chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: Power in Pigalle: honorary police and CIA offers
summary: Butler says he could fix working-paper trouble, was given an honorary police status, and twice turned down offers from the CIA, once when Martin Luther King visited.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Now, I'm staying, I'm dealing, I'm doing a lot of things. Now what happened to me --
What were some of the things you were doing?

Well, I had power, man. Somebody was doing something, like they had trouble with working papers, "Go see so and so." And the police gave me a little--an honorary. I was a policeman, almost, arresting. And I was offered a CI job two times -- FBI.
See, when Martin Luther King was over there, then another time I was offered CIA. So I said, no, I want freedom. /I don't want to be with this.
